title: The delivery payout that quietly shrinks to zero
problem: Delivery payout statements stack commissions, fees and GST so densely that restaurant owners cannot tell what an order earned. A 6-outlet chain lost ₹16 lakh in small, unnotified deductions.
challenge: Catch every wrong deduction on a restaurant's delivery payout the week it lands, with the proof to claim it back.

title: Machine down and the only expert is days away
problem: Small factories halt production for days after a breakdown because nothing connects them quickly with qualified repair technicians. Many technicians on the floor cannot even complete a work order from a phone.
challenge: Get a stalled machine diagnosed within the hour by the people already on the floor.

title: Every 5th appointment is an empty chair
problem: A patient who wants to reschedule can only call in working hours or reply to an SMS nobody reads. An audit of 47 Indian specialist clinics found about 1 in 5 booked appointments end as no-shows.
challenge: Cut a clinic's no-shows in half without adding a single call to the front desk.

title: Cab drivers accept trips blind and earn below cost
problem: Cab drivers cannot see whether a trip is long or short before accepting it. Fares no longer cover running costs on hot days, and fees and penalties take close to 40 percent.
challenge: Show a driver, before accepting, whether a trip will make or lose money after fuel and fees.

title: Hindi Shorts that stall, and nobody explains why
problem: Hindi-speaking creators see their Shorts stall and subscribers stop growing, and nobody says what to change. Their analytics show far more watch hours than YouTube counts towards monetisation, as raised on its help forum on 6 Oct.
challenge: Give a Hindi-speaking creator a weekly note, in Hindi, on what to change next and why.

title: The gateway discount that was promised and never applied
problem: Merchants on Razorpay and Cashfree report fees deducted above the rate they signed for. One merchant raised tickets for 4 months and had the account deactivated before anything was fixed.
challenge: Check every fee a merchant's gateway charged last month against the agreed rate, and recover the overcharge.

title: Interiors promised in 45 days, finished 4 months late
problem: Homeowners pay a large advance, or the whole amount upfront, then wait while interiors work starts late or never starts. Reviews of Livspace and HomeLane describe projects running months over.
challenge: Keep every rupee of an interiors payment back until that stage is finished and photographed.

title: The take-home test AI can now sit for you
problem: Since 2025, take-home coding work has been easy to hand to AI. One instructor moved most of the grade into in-class exams, but live checks only work for a small class.
challenge: Let a teacher check, in 5 minutes per student, that whoever submitted the work actually understands it.

title: Tax notices built on UPI receipts
problem: Small traders received thousands of tax notices based purely on their UPI receipts. They were then asked for years of purchase bills and statements they never kept.
challenge: Turn a small shop's payment history into books that can answer a tax notice in a day.

title: The job post that drowns in generated applications
problem: An open job post can draw hundreds of irrelevant, machine-written applications within hours. One hiring manager gave up and went back to referrals, which shut out good people with no network.
challenge: Let a small employer open a role to anyone and still find the genuine applicants by the end of the first day.

title: Size 32 at one label, 34 at the next
problem: Indian clothing brands borrowed US and UK size charts, so a 32 at one label is a 34 at another. Most shoppers guess, and online fashion returns run at 25–40%, mostly for fit.
challenge: Cut a fashion brand's size returns by a third within one season.

title: Fake seed in a real-looking bag
problem: Counterfeit weedicide and faulty seed reach small farmers through local dealers, and the loss shows only weeks later as a dead crop. Genuine bags look overpriced next to fakes because farmers cannot check what a real product should cost, and the only route to compensation is a court case few can afford.
challenge: Let a farmer check, at the dealer's counter, that a bag of seed or spray is genuine and fairly priced.

title: Weeks of chasing a chatbot for your own money
problem: Refunds for cancelled or undelivered food orders take weeks, and bots block every route to a human. Customers who cannot argue in English are denied outright.
challenge: Get people their refund from a delivery service without them writing a single complaint themselves.

title: Owed lakhs, afraid to ask the buyer for it
problem: About ₹8.1 lakh crore owed to small suppliers sits in overdue buyer payments. Most avoid complaints for fear of losing the customer, and polite reminders get ignored.
challenge: Turn a supplier's overdue invoices into a ready-to-file claim in one evening, without burning the relationship.

title: Every new doctor starts from a folder of X-rays
problem: Hospitals rarely hand over digital copies, so patients carry folders of paper reports and X-rays from doctor to doctor. Complaints from January 2026 describe doctors at a new hospital unable to see past prescriptions or allergies.
challenge: Turn a folder of paper reports into a one-page history any new doctor can read in a minute.

title: The late ride home that starts with fear
problem: Women heading home late avoid autos and cabs, and there is little recourse when a ride goes wrong. In May 2025 a Rapido driver headed away from the railway station.
challenge: Let a woman travelling late know the moment her ride goes off route, and bring help within seconds.

title: The small community losing its feed to bots
problem: Cheap AI-generated posts flooded small online communities in 2025, and they cannot filter bots without asking everyone for a real identity. Checking uploads still needs trusted human moderators that small hosts cannot afford.
challenge: Keep a small community free of bots, spam and unsafe uploads for less than the cost of one moderator.

title: The digital arrest that ends in a UPI transfer
problem: Callers posing as officials tell people they are under digital arrest and pressure them into moving their savings over UPI. Voice clones and deepfake video calls became cheap in 2025.
challenge: Stop a digital arrest scam before the money moves, without locking the target out of their own account.

title: One flat listed, 15 calls a day, years later
problem: Owners with free listings on 99acres and MagicBricks get call after call from sales teams pushing paid upgrades. A former customer still gets over 15 sales calls a day, years after closing the account.
challenge: Let an owner list a property without their real phone number ever reaching a sales team.

title: The sales call promised it, the course denied it
problem: Edtech sales staff promise deferrals, content and mentoring on calls, then the company denies it after payment. Complaints about coaching to the consumer helpline tripled in a year.
challenge: Make every promise on an edtech sales call show up in writing before the buyer pays.

title: Sold on paper, still waiting for the cash
problem: About a quarter of cash-on-delivery orders come back to small online sellers in India. They wait 3–7 days for couriers to hand over cash from the rest, which delays restocking.
challenge: Show a small online seller which orders will turn into cash, and when, before they spend on stock or ads.

title: Nobody remembers why it was built this way
problem: Teams lose the reasons behind past decisions, so new hires spend weeks digging through old tickets to learn why. Work inherited from colleagues who have left arrives with no context and no owner.
challenge: Let anyone ask why a past decision was made and get the reason, the people and the date in seconds.

title: The fake moisturiser you only spot after using it
problem: Counterfeit cosmetics reach buyers through big marketplaces, and buyers often suspect a fake only after using it. In June 2026 a Nykaa buyer worked it out after the return window had closed and was refused a refund.
challenge: Let a buyer tell whether a beauty product is genuine within a minute of unboxing it.

title: Farmer collectives that can grow but cannot sell
problem: Farmer producer organisations default on dues and fail at marketing, with no budget for branding and weak buyer trust. Those that list online stall on cataloguing, labelling and payments that take weeks.
challenge: Let a farmer collective run its selling side without hiring a full-time trading team.

title: One inspection, no hygiene records, licence gone
problem: Small food units keep hygiene and pest-control records on paper or in clunky software, and one inspection exposes the gaps. In September 2026 a food manufacturer lost its licence over pests and no food-safety records.
challenge: Make a small food unit inspection-ready every day with 5 minutes of record keeping.

title: The 9 kg parcel billed as 13 kg
problem: Couriers re-weigh parcels after pickup and bill small online sellers for weight that was never there, sometimes with no photo proof. One seller's 9 kg parcel was charged as 13 kg, and Shiprocket ignored the dispute.
challenge: Give a small seller proof of weight and size that settles the dispute before it starts.

title: A parent's care, arranged from another city
problem: Sole earners living in another city find arranging care for an ageing parent fragmented and stressful. One family was quoted about $20,000 a year for concierge care coordination.
challenge: Let a working child keep a parent's doctors, medicines and helpers on track in 10 minutes a day.

title: Car hosts lose their income to unsettled claims
problem: People who rent out their car through sharing marketplaces wait months or a year for damage, seizure or total-loss payouts. The car sits idle while they wait.
challenge: Help a car host or driver build a claim the marketplace cannot ignore, and track it to payment.

title: A famous face, a fake investment link, real losses
problem: Deepfake videos of well-known public figures push fake investment links, and scams like these surged across India in 2025. Young followers lose money acting on advice they have no easy way to check.
challenge: Help a young investor check a finance video's claims, and who is making them, before they act on it.

title: One gateway freeze can stop a business overnight
problem: Payment providers block online merchants' accounts or hold their money without explanation, sometimes for months. Money already earned stays frozen, and a business with a single provider has nobody to call.
challenge: Keep a small online business taking payments the day its gateway freezes it.

title: The deposit you lose even with photos
problem: At move-out, tenants face heavy deductions from their deposit, photos or not, with no record both sides agreed at handover. Home buyers find seepage, cracks or termites within weeks because proper inspections are rare.
challenge: Make a dated record of a home's condition in 15 minutes that landlord and tenant both sign.

title: Half of job seekers cannot spot a fake recruiter
problem: Most Indian job seekers have met fake job offers, and half cannot tell a genuine recruiter from a scammer. People lose registration fees and months of search time.
challenge: Tell a first-time job seeker within seconds whether an offer, recruiter or posting is real.

title: The billing screen that freezes at the busiest hour
problem: Billing at Indian shop counters freezes during busy hours, and bugs can take 3–4 months to fix. Owners go back to a paper khata for small credit because logging it is too slow, and paper notes get lost.
challenge: Let a shopkeeper record a sale or a credit entry in under 5 seconds, even with no network.

title: Small tweaks and AI hours that never get billed
problem: Freelancers and small agencies lose margin to unbilled client tweaks and retainer hours nobody tracks. No timesheet records the time spent prompting and waiting on AI.
challenge: Show a freelancer, every week, exactly which unbilled work is eating their margin and what to charge for it.

title: The empty box that comes back as a return
problem: Small Meesho fashion sellers find 5–12% of returns come back as wrong or tampered items, and some as empty boxes. Claims must be filed with photo proof within 48–72 hours, and under a quarter succeed without proof of packing.
challenge: Give a small seller proof of what went into every parcel that a marketplace will actually accept.

title: Milk poured daily, incentives paid 4 months late
problem: Nearly 4 lakh farmers who supply Aavin in Tamil Nadu went 4 months without their per-litre incentives. Collectives short of working capital cannot say when members will be paid, so farmers drift to private buyers.
challenge: Make sure every dairy farmer knows, each evening, what they are owed and when it will arrive.

title: The food reel paid for with a free meal
problem: Micro food bloggers are often paid only in free meals because restaurants cannot tell whether a reel brought any paying diner. Small food brands are as lost on ads, where spend returns barely 1.2–1.5x.
challenge: Let a small food creator prove what their last reel sold, and get paid for it.

title: FASTag tolls for a truck that was parked
problem: Several FASTag toll deductions hit one owner's truck while it was parked, and the refund was rejected. Another paid BlackBuck for access to loads, then got no loads for a month and no money back.
challenge: Catch every wrong toll, autopay and fee on a truck owner's account, and get it refunded.

title: The memory slip you can't hear over the phone
problem: Children living far from an ageing parent struggle to notice a slow decline in memory from ordinary phone calls. Y Combinator's 2026 call for startups said almost no technology is built for older people.
challenge: Help a family notice a parent's memory slipping early, and keep that parent safe online meanwhile.

title: The bus that never arrives, and nobody tells you
problem: Intercity buses are cancelled the day before travel, or never reach the boarding point at all, and no one warns the passenger. They find out at the roadside, with no other bus offered and no word on their refund.
challenge: Get a stranded passenger onto the next bus before they've left the stop.

title: Suspended overnight and never told why
problem: Indian creators lose channels and seller accounts overnight for policy breaches nobody names. Appeals vanish without a reply, so a business built over years stops earning.
challenge: Turn a vague suspension notice into a clear, evidence-backed appeal filed in one afternoon.

title: Weeks of setup, then a gateway rejection nobody explains
problem: Small businesses spend weeks integrating a payment gateway, then get rejected for their line of business with no clear reason. One waited over a month for activation, unable to take payments online.
challenge: Get a small business approved to take payments online at the first attempt.

title: A paid listing, hundreds of hits, no real tenant
problem: Landlords on paid listing plans see hundreds of hits and not a single genuine tenant enquiry. In June 2026 an owner who bought a MagicBricks premium plan got no genuine tenant or buyer enquiries.
challenge: Sort a landlord's rental enquiries into real tenants and noise before anyone picks up the phone.

title: Good marks, but can't fix a bug
problem: Most engineering and MBA graduates of 2026 are still unplaced. Employers say fresh graduates with good marks cannot debug code or apply what they learnt, because colleges teach mostly theory.
challenge: Let a graduate from a small college prove one real skill to an employer in a single afternoon.

title: 2 lakh kiranas closed in a single year
problem: A kirana needs hundreds of loyal households to survive on thin margins, so losing a handful can close it. A retailer federation says 2 lakh kiranas closed in a year.
challenge: Help a kirana keep its loyal households ordering from it rather than from the nearest dark store.

title: 150 applications, 2 interviews, and not one reason why
problem: Hiring filters never show what they read or why they said no, so job seekers guess and burn out. One job seeker sent around 150 applications and got 2 interviews.
challenge: Tell a job seeker, with evidence, why their applications stall and the one change to make next.

title: A confirmed salon slot, and still a half-hour wait
problem: Salon bookings kept by hand ignore how long each service takes, so customers with a confirmed slot still wait half an hour. Indian salons lose 4–5 appointments a day to no-shows, over ₹70,000 a month.
challenge: Cut a salon's no-shows and waiting time in half without adding a receptionist.

title: Crops ploughed under because the mandi offered ₹2
problem: Small growers sell into the one market within reach, often at ₹2 to ₹8 a kilo, less than it cost to grow. Prices swing by half within days, and nobody tells a grower where a better buyer is a few hours away.
challenge: Tell a small grower, before harvest day, where and when their crop will fetch the most.

title: One viral reel and the home bakery breaks
problem: A single viral post can flood a small food seller with more orders than its stock and hands can manage. Customised celebration cakes arrive hours late or damaged, ruining birthdays.
challenge: Help a home food seller say yes to the right number of orders and deliver every one intact.

title: The carrier who collects the load, then vanishes
problem: Hundreds of carriers and brokers can register at a single mailbox address, and carrier numbers are cheap, so a shipper cannot tell a real carrier from an impostor. Cargo theft through spoofed identities rose sharply in 2025 and 2026, faster than the manual checks brokers rely on. Brokers are still liable for poor vetting, with no quick way to check who they are handing a load to.
challenge: Tell a shipper within a minute whether the carrier on the phone is who they claim to be.

title: The meal nobody logs, and the coach advising blind
problem: Online nutrition coaches advise from clients' food logs, but typing every meal is a chore, so they see half the picture. Coaches have posted the same complaint in reviews from May 2025 to September 2026.
challenge: Let a client log a whole day of meals in under a minute, and the coach see it the same day.

title: Paid in full, and the hotel has no record
problem: Travellers arrive with a paid voucher to find the hotel has no record of them, or no room. In August 2026 a corporate booking for 4 guests was recorded as 1, forcing a large extra charge at the desk.
challenge: Make sure the hotel knows about a paid booking, with the right guests, before the traveller arrives.

title: Labelled AI-made, and the creator cannot take it off
problem: Automatic labels for synthetic media rolled out across the major video services in 2025, and they catch genuine work: in October 2026 a creator's green-screen video was tagged as AI-generated and the label locked. Crackdowns on machine-made content now bury faceless creators however much effort they put in, while a fully synthetic influencer gathered millions of followers who believed she was real.
challenge: Let a creator prove a piece of work is theirs and human-made, in a way any viewer can check in seconds.

title: The claim rejected over a clause nobody explained
problem: Over half of Indian health insurance claimants face rejection or partial approval, often over exclusions or paperwork they did not understand. Premiums have jumped 50–200% in 3 years.
challenge: Help a family get a health claim paid in full on the first submission.

title: Paid for inspections, and nobody ever came
problem: Landlords pay for property management, then get no showings, no inspections and a manager who goes silent. One owner paying NoBroker a percentage fee in October 2026 got no inspections and missing tenant documents.
challenge: Give a distant landlord proof, every month, that someone visited and checked their flat.

title: Paid for the course, then the company went silent
problem: Learners pay for courses, books and certificates, then the books never arrive or the classes freeze right before exams. One online degree provider took a ₹10,000 reservation fee, rejected the applicant and kept the money.
challenge: Get a stranded learner their money back, or a written answer, within 2 weeks of the first complaint.

title: Fake cash-on-delivery orders bleeding small sellers
problem: Small online sellers lose around ₹600 on every fake or refused cash-on-delivery order once shipping and ad spend are counted. Competitors place such orders on purpose, and the add-ons meant to catch them break for days.
challenge: Stop fake cash-on-delivery orders before they ship, without turning away real first-time buyers.

title: Sold on the demo, still not live months later
problem: Mid-size firms buy HR and payroll packages on the strength of a demo, then find limits the demo hid and an implementation team that stops replying. One company was still not live 2.5 months after buying, with no manuals, and configuring approvals and forms in-house is slow. Staff come to hate what they paid for, and a refund promised during the sale never arrived.
challenge: Get a mid-size firm live on new HR and payroll in 2 weeks, with every approval flow tested first.

title: Bridal slots booked in DMs, lost to ghosting
problem: Freelance makeup artists, mehendi artists and saree drapers take bookings through direct messages with no deposit, contract or trial. One ghosted wedding slot wipes out a full day's income.
challenge: Make booking a freelance beauty professional as binding as booking a salon, with a deposit, a trial and a findable profile.

title: Growers get ₹5–7 a kilo, kitchens pay retail
problem: Onion and potato growers get barely 43% of the retail price, and mandi rates have crashed to ₹5–7 a kilo. Restaurants nearby pay retail for the same produce, because wholesalers want bigger minimum orders than they can store.
challenge: Connect small growers to the kitchens near them, with orders sized for both and paid within the week.

title: Card money that never reaches the restaurant
problem: Restaurants need same-day cash for suppliers and wages, yet money from card sales arrives late. After a change of bank details, some payments stop arriving at all and support cannot trace them.
challenge: Tell a restaurant owner every morning which payments are due, which are late, and who to chase.

title: Every small export order carries a big exporter's paperwork
problem: Small exporters carry the same paperwork as the biggest, and matching many small export receipts to bank entries is slow. Labelling rules reported in September 2026 add more proof to every shipment.
challenge: Close every small export's paperwork and bank entries within a week of payment, without a full-time clerk.

title: Booked, travelled, and the doctor is on leave
problem: Patients book a specialist online, travel there and find the doctor on leave or the clinic shut, with no warning. Reports like these run from November 2025 to August 2026.
challenge: Make sure a patient who books a doctor finds that doctor, at that place, at that price.

title: The fare you only learn when the ride ends
problem: In a 2025 survey, 59% of ride-hailing riders faced charges added only at the end of the trip. One rider paid about 4 times the estimated fare for the same route.
challenge: Tell a rider before booking what this trip should cost, and flag the overcharge before they pay.

title: Brand money stops at the metro limits
problem: 2 in 3 Indian creators come from smaller cities, yet brand spend still flows mostly to metro creators. Most land only 1 paid campaign a year, so creating rarely becomes an income.
challenge: Help a small-town creator land their second paid campaign this quarter, not next year.

title: Scammed over UPI, and the money never comes back
problem: 1 in 5 Indian families that use UPI has been hit by fraud in 3 years. Half of victims never complained because reporting felt pointless or complicated.
challenge: Get a scam victim's complaint filed everywhere it matters within the first hour.

title: Wiring a deposit to someone who cloned the listing
problem: Scammers clone real rental listings, impersonate the owner and collect deposits for homes that are not for rent. A deposit is often a month or more of savings.
challenge: Let a renter confirm, before sending any money, that the person asking for it really controls the home.

title: Patient one-on-one tutoring is still for the few
problem: Most young children learn reading and arithmetic without patient one-on-one help. Parents have no child-safe controls over what an AI assistant says, and were asking for them as early as May 2025.
challenge: Give a young child a patient voice tutor whose every answer a parent can limit and review.

title: Your own business records, held hostage by the vendor
problem: Small firms depend on vendors and implementation partners to reach their own records. In November 2025 a partner deleted a company's Odoo database without permission.
challenge: Get a small business's records out of any old setup into a file it owns, in an afternoon.

title: Every HR change waits for the one admin
problem: HR software is so complex that routine reports still need an admin to step in. HR managers, recruiters and analysts have said so in reviews from April to September 2026.
challenge: Let any manager change an HR workflow or pull a report by describing it in one sentence, without the admin.

title: The foundation shade that turns wrong by noon
problem: Indian buyers often order several wrong foundation shades online, because undertone does not show in a product photo. The shade turns wrong within hours, and every wrong bottle is money wasted.
challenge: Help someone find a shade and a routine that work on their skin before they spend a rupee.

title: Pest advice that arrives after the crop is gone
problem: Farmers struggle to get timely crop and cattle advice in their regional language, so a vet visit costs money and days. Pest attacks come without early warning, sprays are applied by guesswork, and residues end up in food.
challenge: Give a farmer a trustworthy answer about a sick plant or animal, in their language, within the hour.

title: Every rupee of the menu price already spoken for
problem: Owner-run restaurants were hit by rising ingredient, labour and rent costs in 2025, on top of taxes, card fees and aggregator commissions. Card fees alone push owners to raise menu prices or add charges that annoy diners.
challenge: Show a restaurant owner, dish by dish, where the money goes and which change would save the most this month.

title: The shipping wallet that eats a seller's cash
problem: Small online sellers prepay shipping into a courier wallet, then watch unexplained deductions and disputed weight charges eat that money. In July 2026 a frozen wallet stopped one seller from shipping at all.
challenge: Show a small seller every rupee the courier holds or took, and get the wrong ones back within a week.

title: A hospital bill with nothing to check it against
problem: Patients get long itemised hospital bills with no upfront price for a routine procedure to compare against. Courts and regulators pushed Indian hospitals to publish standard rates in 2024 and 2025, yet the bill still comes first.
challenge: Tell a patient before admission what a routine procedure should cost, and flag what does not belong on the bill.

title: Drivers cancel the moment they see your destination
problem: In a 2026 survey, 82% of ride-hailing riders had faced driver cancellations. One rider waited over 20 minutes for a driver who then refused the trip.
challenge: Get a rider to the airport on time even when 3 drivers cancel in a row.

title: The influencer budget nobody can prove paid off
problem: 2 in 5 brands say they cannot measure return on influencer campaigns. Agencies spend hours every week exporting ad data, cleaning it and building client reports in spreadsheets.
challenge: Show a brand what each creator campaign returned, in a report nobody has to build by hand.

title: Paid in 90 days, paying their vendors in 30
problem: Small suppliers wait 60–90 days or more for big buyers to pay, while paying their own vendors in 30. They borrow at high interest to cover the gap, and one spent 6 months chasing a single delayed payment.
challenge: Shorten the gap between delivery and payment for a small supplier by a month.

title: The quote that grows once the advance is paid
problem: Painting and interior jobs start with a low quote that grows with extras once work begins. In September 2026 one interiors firm took a ₹1 lakh advance, then quoted many times the original estimate.
challenge: Turn any interiors or painting quote into a fair-price check a homeowner can take back to the contractor the same day.

title: 100 applications, 7 interviews, and no feedback
problem: One candidate got interviews from only 7 of 100 applications, and new graduates hear almost nothing back. Candidates lose track of where they applied, submit twice and miss follow-ups.
challenge: Turn a graduate's next 50 applications into 20 targeted ones that each get a reply.

title: Same van, same costs, 50 shops instead of 80
problem: Metro consumer-goods distributors are losing 10 to 25% of snack and beverage volume to quick commerce. Their vans now serve 50 kiranas instead of 80 while costs stay fixed.
challenge: Help a distributor win back revenue per route, or cut the cost of serving each shop, by a fifth.

title: The sync that broke 3 payroll cycles ago
problem: Scheduled jobs can report success while doing nothing, and teams find out hours later if at all. One HR team typed in leave by hand for 61 staff across 3 payroll cycles after a sync quietly broke.
challenge: Tell a small team within the hour when data that should have moved between their services did not.

title: Bought from the official store, delivered as a fake
problem: 40% of Indian cosmetics buyers have hit counterfeits in 3 years, with online platforms the top source. A quarter of them reported allergic reactions.
challenge: Show a beauty buyer where a specific unit came from before it touches their skin.

title: Fruit that rots between the field and the buyer
problem: Up to 15 percent of fruit and 12 percent of vegetables are lost between harvest and sale. Perishable shipments are delayed or damaged in transit with no record, so claims go nowhere.
challenge: Make it cheaper for a grower to hold, grade or ship a perishable crop than to dump it.

title: Too big for retail, too small for wholesale
problem: Small restaurants pay suppliers more because vendors discount only committed, prepaid orders. An owner works 14-hour shifts and keeps almost nothing once ingredients, wages and rent are paid.
challenge: Get a small kitchen or a big household wholesale prices without prepaying for a truckload.

title: Broken in transit, and the claim takes forever
problem: A few percent of online sellers' parcels are lost or damaged in transit, and fragile goods suffer most. Claims drag on for weeks or are denied for lack of evidence, and the seller usually takes the loss.
challenge: Get a seller paid for a broken or lost parcel in days, not weeks.

title: Wrong medicine at the door, and the return refused
problem: A wrong medicine is refused for return because the buyer supposedly checked it on delivery. Complaints sit unresolved for months.
challenge: Let a patient know, before accepting a delivery, that a medicine is the right drug, in date and genuine.

title: Airline refunded weeks ago, and the money never arrived
problem: Airlines release refunds for cancelled flights to online travel agents, who hold them for weeks before anything reaches the traveller. Train passengers delayed 3 hours or more see refund claims rejected on technical grounds.
challenge: Get every refund a traveller is owed into their account without them writing a single email.

title: Lakhs owed, and the brand pays when it likes
problem: Indian creators routinely wait over 2 months for brands to pay. Creators under half a million followers negotiate, invoice and chase alone, so many refuse new work without a 25–50% advance.
challenge: Get a creator paid on time for brand work without a single awkward reminder.

title: Foreign client paid, freelancer still waiting
problem: Freelancers earning from abroad see payouts held for days and accounts blocked over address typos or missed OTPs. Surprise fees and poor conversion routes shave off more.
challenge: Get an Indian freelancer's foreign earnings into their bank on a predictable day, at a known cost.

title: Paying an inspection fee to hear an inflated quote
problem: Appliance technicians charge an inspection fee, then push replacement parts nobody can check, at inflated prices. In September 2026, an AC repair booked through Urban Company was allegedly misdiagnosed.
challenge: Give a household a second opinion on a repair quote before they say yes to the technician.

title: ₹2.5 lakh on a data course, and zero interviews
problem: Learners pay lakhs for tech and data courses sold with placement guarantees, then meet weak teaching and silent support. One paid about ₹2.5 lakh and had zero interviews 3 months after finishing.
challenge: Show a learner, before they pay, what the last batch of a course actually went on to do.

title: Sold out of fast sellers, stuck with slow ones
problem: Kirana owners reorder hundreds of items by gut feel, running out of fast sellers while slow stock ties up cash. Small shops live on turning stock, and one bookshop has to turn its shelves 4–5 times a year to cover fixed costs.
challenge: Make the weekly reorder take 10 minutes and leave fewer empty shelves and fewer dusty ones.

title: The support ticket that holds up everyone's salary
problem: Small teams get support requests across chat, code trackers and email, so urgent ones wait behind trivial ones. A query stuck with an HR provider's support during payroll week can stop salaries going out.
challenge: Answer a small team's routine support questions in minutes, and get the urgent ones to a person first.

title: The lipstick arrived opened, and the return was refused
problem: Beauty and grocery buyers cannot see a manufacturing or best-before date before ordering. Skincare has arrived with 13 of its 24 months of shelf life already gone.
challenge: Make a beauty order's shelf life and seal visible before payment, and provable after delivery.

title: The farm ledger nobody finishes setting up
problem: Farm accounting packages need setting up before they do anything useful, and entering records is a chore. In September 2026, women-led farmer producer companies were reported shutting down once grants ended.
challenge: Turn a farm's receipts and purchases into usable books on the first day, with no setup.

title: The restaurant that can't call its own regulars
problem: Delivery aggregators hide customer details, so a restaurant cannot build direct ties with its own customers. In 2025 aggregators launched their own food brands, and restaurants fear their order data will be used against them.
challenge: Help a small restaurant turn one-time delivery customers into regulars who order direct.

title: Pickup today, says the message, every day
problem: Small sellers get repeated pickup-scheduled messages while no courier arrives, so dispatch slips for days and buyers get angry. Prepaid shipping is not refunded, and some shipments show no movement for weeks.
challenge: Make sure a booked pickup happens the same day, or a different courier comes.

title: The claim rejected, and nobody will say why
problem: Over 40% of surveyed Indian policyholders say health claims were rejected or only part paid for reasons they consider invalid. Nobody explains the decision.
challenge: Help a family fight a rejected health claim with the right clause and the right letter, in one evening.

title: The bus moved and nobody told the passenger
problem: Intercity buses change pickup points by phone, run hours late or leave while booked passengers are minutes away. Live tracking and driver contact numbers are often wrong, so passengers miss buses and lose the fare.
challenge: Make sure every passenger knows where and when their bus really is, before they leave home.

title: The blog worth reading that search no longer shows
problem: Independent blogs and niche forums have become hard to find through mainstream search. Since AI answers began replacing clicks in 2025, staying visible takes a huge content effort with uncertain returns.
challenge: Get a small independent writer found by the readers already searching for exactly what they write.

title: The fees on your statement you never agreed to
problem: Indian cardholders unknowingly pay thousands of crores in surprise annual fees, late fees and add-ons buried in their statements. Most bank customers find them hard to spot or reverse.
challenge: Find every fee a household paid this year that it could have avoided, and get it reversed.

title: Paid to avoid brokers, and still calling brokers
problem: Renters pay for owner-only plans and still get handed broker numbers, as one paying house hunter reported in September 2026. Many attractive listings are broker bait, with borrowed photos or homes that are not available.
challenge: Flag a broker posing as an owner, or a borrowed photo, before a renter makes the call.

title: College advice paid for by the colleges
problem: School leavers in India get college advice from counsellors who earn referral commissions, steering them towards costly private colleges. A wrong choice costs years and lakhs of rupees.
challenge: Give a school leaver advice on what to study next that no college has paid to influence.

title: Card fees and add-ons eating a shop's margin
problem: Small retailers pay flat processing fees plus a monthly charge for nearly every point-of-sale feature. One shop spends about $400 a month on card fees, and basic stock valuation reports cost extra.
challenge: Show a small retailer exactly what payments and software cost per sale, and how to cut it.

title: The answer is in someone's head, and they're away
problem: Team know-how sits in a few heads and old chat threads, so work stalls when that person is away. Threads from April 2025 to April 2026 keep finding that documentation never catches up unless it happens on its own.
challenge: Keep a team's know-how written down as a side effect of the work it already does, with nobody editing a wiki.

title: A quarter of a shopkeeper's wage, for handwoven cloth
problem: A March 2025 report found Indian handloom weavers earn a quarter of what shopkeepers do, losing margin to middlemen. Selling online means website builders that assume design and technical skills they do not have.
challenge: Let a weaver list a piece for sale online from a phone, in their regional language, in 5 minutes.

title: Signed up for carbon credits, and never paid
problem: Farmers in private carbon programmes do not know what they will earn or when. A December 2024 study found nearly all farmers in voluntary carbon projects received no payment.
challenge: Show every enrolled farmer what their fields have earned, why, and when the money arrives.

title: 6 fees stacked on top of one meal
problem: A meal on a delivery service can cost nearly double what the restaurant's own site charges. One delivery receipt in September 2026 stacked 6 separate fees on top of the food.
challenge: Show a hungry customer the true total for the same order across every way of buying it, before they pay.

title: The idle truck nobody puts a price on
problem: Indian fleet owners rarely track the time a vehicle is off the road, one of their largest hidden expenses. A 2026 interface update forced one fleet team to retrain the staff who log inspections and repairs.
challenge: Show a fleet owner what each idle day costs in rupees, without anyone typing in more data.

title: The home exercises nobody does once sessions end
problem: Clients tend to stop their home exercises once paid sessions end, and coaches cannot compare what was prescribed with what was done. In July 2026 a paid coach's client got only forwarded YouTube videos and no follow-up.
challenge: Show a coach which clients actually did this week's exercises, and how well, without a single extra call.

title: Airline refunded in full, traveller got ₹1,750 less
problem: Online travel agents keep their convenience fee even when the airline cancels, and pass on less than the airline paid back. In April 2026 one airline refunded the agent in full, and the traveller got about ₹1,750 less.
challenge: Show a traveller exactly what the airline refunded, and make sure every rupee of it reaches them.

title: Money stuck, and only a bot will answer
problem: Creator and payment services moved most of their support to bots in 2025. One link-in-bio service kept taking payments a creator never authorised while its support bot said the account did not exist.
challenge: Get a small seller's stuck money or broken account in front of a human who can fix it, within a day.

title: The GST notice: pay it, or reply to it?
problem: Small taxpayers get GST demand notices and do not know whether to pay or reply. A wrong guess risks penalties, and as of July 2026 e-way bill rules keep changing too.
challenge: Tell a small business what a notice means, what to file and by when, in its regional language, within the hour.

title: The token amount that never comes back
problem: Renters pay a token advance to hold a flat, then the owner backs out or rents it to someone else. The refund stays pending for months, and chasing a small sum costs more than it is worth.
challenge: Make a rental token refundable by default, released only when both sides confirm the deal.

title: A year of exam prep, paid upfront
problem: Exam-prep courses demand non-refundable yearly fees upfront, with no way to pay per topic or try first. Students on tight budgets pay for a year they may never use.
challenge: Let an exam aspirant pay only for the topics and weeks they actually use.

title: One flag and a seller's balance is gone
problem: Small online sellers depend on a few marketplaces and payment providers that can close an account overnight. Their balance can stay frozen for months, sometimes after one unusually large sale.
challenge: Keep a small seller trading and paid on the day one marketplace or payment provider freezes them.

title: Decided in the chat, never on the task list
problem: Small teams decide things in chat threads that never reach the task list, and spoken promises are forgotten. In one 2025 case, staff moved real discussions into personal WhatsApp groups, scattering decisions.
challenge: Turn every promise made in a chat or a call into a task with an owner and a date, the same day.

title: Hand-counted commissions, and the disputes that follow
problem: Indian salon owners still work out staff commissions and attendance by hand, which keeps causing disputes. They also spend over 10 hours a month on GST reconciliation.
challenge: Make a salon's month-end close, commissions and GST included, take an hour and end with no staff disputes.

title: The watermelon nobody could trace
problem: When a family in Mumbai died after eating a contaminated watermelon, nobody could trace where it came from. In July 2026 cakes ordered online arrived stale with no record of when they were made.
challenge: Let a fruit seller or small food maker prove where and when their food was grown or made, for paise a label.

title: Infested kitchens, and diners order blind
problem: A September 2026 inspection drive in Hyderabad found infestations, expired stock and poor handler hygiene in most of the restaurants it checked. Diners ordering online still have no way to see a kitchen's hygiene before they pay.
challenge: Let a diner see how clean a kitchen is before ordering, in a way the kitchen cannot fake.

title: No paid seat, no way to log the fault
problem: A chemical plant could afford only a few MaintainX licences, so everyone else logs work through someone who has one. Software for maintenance crews has barely changed in 20 years.
challenge: Let anyone on the shop floor log a fault in 10 seconds, without a paid seat.

title: Clinics pay lakhs for listings that bring one patient
problem: Indian doctors pay booking marketplaces tens of thousands to lakhs a year for visibility. They get a handful of leads or none, and terms change without notice.
challenge: Show a small clinic exactly which rupee of its marketing brought which patient.

title: The flexible fare that wasn't, and a no-show instead
problem: Flexible fares, travel insurance and baggage allowances are sold at checkout and then not honoured. Travel agents were asked to audit pre-ticked add-ons in 2025, yet complaints kept coming through 2026.
challenge: Tell a traveller, before they pay, exactly what each add-on will and will not cover.

title: 11 weeks in monetisation review, and nobody to ask
problem: Creators who cross the monetisation thresholds can wait months in review. One has waited over 11 weeks for a re-review with no timeline from support.
challenge: Tell a creator where their monetisation stands and what to fix next, in plain words, in under a minute.

title: Prising ledgers out of Tally piece by piece
problem: Accountants pull ledgers out of TallyPrime piece by piece to analyse them, which is slow and lets errors in. Elsewhere, a bookkeeper can bulk-update only 25 items at a time, so hours go on repetitive edits.
challenge: Get every ledger out of Tally in one clean pull, ready to analyse in minutes rather than a day.

title: 6 months' rent upfront, and cuts nobody explains
problem: Bengaluru brokers still demand 6 months of rent upfront. At move-out, inspection teams inflate repair costs, and tenants lose money they have no way to contest.
challenge: Give a tenant a deposit statement they can contest line by line before they hand back the keys.

title: Parents pay the tutor and never see the learning
problem: Parents pay for tuition and get no proof their child is learning. In September 2026 one parent paying for online coding and maths classes reported no visible progress at all.
challenge: Let a tutor show every parent what their child learnt this week, in the time it takes to pack up.

title: Over-order and block cash, or run out of stock
problem: Shop owners cannot see what their suppliers have in stock, so they over-order and block cash, or run out. In August 2024 a retailer who bought rice wholesale online got poor-quality stock and had the return rejected.
challenge: Let a shopkeeper know what will arrive, and at what price, before the money leaves their hand.

title: Your fingers are the slowest part of the job
problem: Much of a working day now goes on writing messages and prompts. For people who chat with AI heavily, typing speed is the limit, and the drive to work is lost time.
challenge: Let someone clear their inbox and draft every reply by voice before they reach the office.

title: Years of size charts you cannot take with you
problem: Small clothing stores on Shopify pay per-order fees for size-chart add-ons, so fit guidance costs more as sales grow. One merchant could not export years of charts they had built.
challenge: Give a small clothing store fit guidance it owns, that never silently breaks and costs nothing per order.

title: Queueing for urea, then paying above the subsidised price
problem: Farmers in Telangana queue for urea with no reliable word on which dealer has stock, then pay above the subsidised price. Nearly 3 in 4 small cattle rearers also struggle to get affordable fodder.
challenge: Show a farmer which dealer has urea today, at the fair price, before they leave home.

title: Spices, water and milk nobody can vouch for
problem: Families distrust packaged spice powders for adulteration and staleness, yet grinding fresh at home takes effort. They cannot tell whether a 20-litre water can is truly purified, or find the fat content of packaged milk and whether powder went into it. Every claim on the label has to be taken on trust, every day.
challenge: Help a family check its spices, water and milk at home in under 5 minutes.

title: Decades-old code, and nobody left who can fix it
problem: Small family businesses depend on custom code written decades ago that nobody left can repair. As late as 2025 freight, travel and banking firms still ran on old terminal systems.
challenge: Get a small firm off its old custom code, books intact, without stopping the business for a day.

title: Therapists write reports in the hours they should rest
problem: An autism services worker writes very long insurance reports every 6 months, with almost no time set aside for them. Staff at mid-sized Indian clinics spend about 11 hours a week on calls, paperwork and bills.
challenge: Turn a therapist's session notes into a progress report ready to send before the next session starts.

title: Peer car rental runs on trust nobody can check
problem: Self-drive renters are blacklisted without reason, listings use fake registration numbers, and hosts fail to hand over cars. Deposits and damage refunds stay pending for months.
challenge: Let a renter and a car owner verify each other and settle deposits without a third party.

title: Payout dates that move without a reason
problem: Payout dates slip by a full month, or an account is suspended the day before money is due. Creators who budget around these payments cannot plan rent, equipment or the next shoot.
challenge: Show every creator when each rupee they have earned will land, and raise the alarm the day it slips.

title: Ticking bank lines against the ledger, one by one
problem: Small firms still match their ledgers to the bank by hand, and it remains the slowest part of bookkeeping. In September 2026 one firm found transactions missing from its bank feed, and support could not fix it.
challenge: Match a small firm's month of bank lines to its ledger, leaving a person only the ones that need judgement.

title: Proving what was damaged and what it was worth
problem: Homeowners facing insurance claims must photograph and value every possession, a tedious job taking many hours. Without proof of what existed and what it cost, claims are cut or refused.
challenge: Help a household build a valued, photographed inventory of its home in under an hour.

title: Stuck on one problem with no one to ask
problem: Coaching students say only a few learners ever get live doubt sessions, despite repeated requests. Outside paid tutors or office hours, a student stuck on a textbook problem has nowhere to turn.
challenge: Get a stuck student from a photo of the problem to understanding it, without handing them the answer.

title: The shop that cannot say what went missing
problem: In April 2025 a retailer found stock mismatches varied wildly from store to store, because staff counted carelessly. Small shop owners have stopped reporting shoplifting, so the losses go unrecorded.
challenge: Make a full stock count take an hour and come out right, so a shop knows exactly what went missing.

title: Code is cheap; knowing what to build is not
problem: Since coding agents made building cheap in 2025, the hard part is deciding what to build. Inside companies, every client request arrives labelled top priority, so product managers get noise instead of evidence.
challenge: Turn a pile of customer requests and public complaints into a ranked list of what to build, with the evidence attached.

title: Destroying good clothes because nobody saw demand coming
problem: Garment makers produce on guesswork and lose heavily every year to unsold stock and clearance discounts. Some brands destroy wearable clothes rather than discount them, to protect their prices.
challenge: Help a small apparel maker cut next season's unsold stock by a fifth.

title: Ghee that arrives already expired and growing fungus
problem: In a June 2026 survey, 48% of Indian online grocery shoppers could not see best-before dates before checkout. Ghee from a quick-commerce store arrived already expired and growing fungus.
challenge: Catch every expired or undated pack before it reaches a customer's door.

title: Fixed-price orders meet metal prices that never sit still
problem: Small engineering, plastics and component makers quote fixed prices weeks before buying aluminium, copper, steel or polymer. Input costs then jump, and margins on orders already won vanish.
challenge: Help a small manufacturer quote and buy so that a price spike cannot wipe out an order.

title: One coach, a separate payment link for every package
problem: Online coaches need a separate payment link for every package, and clients cannot see when a session is free. Such complaints came from 3 different coaches in 3 days of July 2026.
challenge: Let a solo coach sell any package, take payment and fill the calendar from one link they share.

title: Driver cancels, and the rider pays the fee
problem: Drivers demand more than the fare shown, in one case nearly 50% more, then cancel when the rider refuses. The rider is charged the cancellation fee.
challenge: Make sure the person who cancels a ride is the one who pays for it.

title: Hijacked channels and a support desk that cannot help
problem: When a creator account is hijacked, recovery options are already changed and support cannot restore access. A small media team can lose a channel it spent years building, along with its earnings.
challenge: Get a locked-out creator back in control within days, and make the next takeover far harder to pull off.

title: Flying blind on next month's cash
problem: Standard small-business accounting software has no basic cash forecast, so owners build spreadsheet workarounds. In July 2026 merchants found their payouts landing later than expected, which made cash planning harder still.
challenge: Show a small owner, each morning, how much cash they will have in 30 days.

title: Nobody will come to fix one switchboard
problem: Electricians prefer big contracts, so homeowners cannot get one to come for a small job like a fan or switchboard. Small faults linger for weeks, and a night-time plumbing emergency means paying inflated rates.
challenge: Get a household's small repair diagnosed by video and either fixed by them or by someone nearby today.

title: The best courses are only in English
problem: Bright students outside big cities miss top online courses because most are available only in English. Indian-language speech models matured in 2025, yet good teaching rarely arrives in the language a learner thinks in.
challenge: Turn one strong English course into one a student who thinks in an Indian language learns from just as well.

title: Packaging costs and rules that shut out tiny sellers
problem: Indian beauty brands saw packaging component costs jump 60 to 70% within weeks in March 2026, before they could raise prices. Customers open single small items in boxes far too big for them, stuffed with plastic.
challenge: Cut a small seller's packaging cost and paperwork per order by a third, at home and abroad.

title: Customers who never say what went wrong
problem: Local service businesses hear almost nothing back from customers, because long surveys go unanswered. Yet many Indian customers today prefer to talk in voice notes, not forms.
challenge: Get a local business honest feedback from a third of its customers, for under 30 seconds of their time.

title: The dress that looks nothing like its photo
problem: Clothes bought online often arrive in an off colour, thinner fabric or a worse fit than the photos showed. One Meesho buyer of a poor-quality dress waited 20 days with no reply to their return request.
challenge: Let a shopper judge fabric, colour and build quality before paying, from evidence rather than the seller's photos.

title: Labels that hide the sugar and the milk
problem: Health-conscious shoppers struggle to tell how much sugar a packaged snack holds, because the labels are hard to read. In December 2025 most parents said they wanted clear red warnings on the front of the pack.
challenge: Let a parent know in one glance whether a packaged food is right for their child.

title: Chasing suppliers by phone, one invoice at a time
problem: In a June 2026 LocalCircles survey, about 2 in 3 MSMEs said they struggle to manage multiple suppliers. Half reported constant follow-ups and invoices that fail GST checks, blocking their input credit.
challenge: Take supplier follow-ups and invoice fixes off a small owner's phone, so no input credit is lost to a bad bill.

title: The same strip of tablets costs half next door
problem: The same prescription can cost 30 to 50% more at one pharmacy than another, and patients cannot compare. Online orders are approved, then cancelled days later because the partner shop never had the stock.
challenge: Tell a patient where their prescription is in stock today, nearby, and at the lowest price.

title: Holding the licence and losing the dispute anyway
problem: Creators who paid for a stock music licence still get Content ID claims, unlisted videos and rejected disputes. In October 2026 one claim hit a Short with hundreds of thousands of views.
challenge: Make a creator's proof of rights impossible to ignore, attached and ready the moment a claim lands.

title: Evenings lost to chasing invoices by hand
problem: Micro businesses spend 10 or more hours a week making, chasing and matching invoices by hand. Contractors lose their evenings chasing what they are owed instead of being with family.
challenge: Get a small owner paid on time without a single evening spent chasing.

title: Paying in full before anyone checks the work
problem: Deep cleaning varies wildly, with missed areas and no checklist or way to check the work. In September 2026 a harsh acid ruined a bathroom's chrome fittings and left the taps leaking, with no remedy offered.
challenge: Let a household sign off a cleaning or carpentry job from before-and-after photos before the final payment.

title: A course business the host can cut overnight
problem: Course creators build years of income on teaching marketplaces and hosts that can change terms at will. One educator was removed without notice, and the audience and income belong to the host, not the teacher.
challenge: Let a course creator move their students, content and payments to a home they own in one weekend.

title: On ONDC, then no orders once the discounts stop
problem: About 85% of shops that joined ONDC never do meaningful business on it. Retail orders fell about 35% from their peak once buyer discounts ended.
challenge: Get a small shop its first 10 repeat online orders without paying for discounts.

title: Automations that break more than the work they replace
problem: Work automations break often or take more setup than the task itself. So people keep repeating the same tedious steps every day, and say they would pay for something dependable.
challenge: Let an office worker hand over one daily chore by showing it once, and have it still work next month.

title: Clothes that stop fitting after a handful of washes
problem: Mass-market garments lose their shape within a handful of washes. Cotton-spandex blends shrink badly even when washed cold and hung to dry, so a correctly sized purchase stops fitting within weeks.
challenge: Tell a shopper how a garment will survive washing, and how to wash it, before it is ruined.

title: Home bakers pricing by gut, selling at a loss
problem: Home bakers price by gut feel without tracking what ingredients cost, and many sell at a loss without knowing it. Tiffin services serve the same fixed menu every day, with no way to swap a dish.
challenge: Let a home cook take an order, price every dish at a profit and handle swaps, all from a phone.

title: Load boards full of stale and phantom freight
problem: One-truck operators pay rising subscriptions for load boards that show stale posts and the same load reposted by competing brokers. New carriers cannot get booked for months.
challenge: Help a one-truck carrier find real, bookable loads without paying for noise.

title: Fitness plans easy to buy, impossible to cancel
problem: Diet and fitness programmes refuse refunds, hide deadlines in the terms and keep billing after cancellation. Members and even trainers report being charged months after they tried to leave.
challenge: Make cancelling a fitness or diet subscription take one minute and leave a record the seller cannot dispute.

title: The counter-notice that hands your details to the harasser
problem: A creator fighting a false copyright strike must send a counter-notice that gives the attacker their personal details. In October 2026 a gaming creator took 3 strikes in a day from someone posing as a game publisher.
challenge: Help a creator beat a false strike within a day without giving the attacker their personal details.

title: The chargeback you had proof for, and still lost
problem: Small online merchants lose chargeback disputes they could have won, because writing a reply with evidence is slow and confusing. In September 2026 one merchant with proof got no response from the gateway's support team.
challenge: Turn a merchant's order and delivery records into a chargeback reply that wins, in minutes rather than an evening.

title: Paid rental search: 1 viewing in 20 days
problem: Renters pay for premium search plans promising dozens of matching homes, then get 1 viewing in 20 days, or none. A Housing.com buyer got a few suggestions across a whole 45-day plan.
challenge: Get a renter 5 real viewings that match their brief within a week.

title: 6 months of job-portal premium, a handful of calls
problem: Indian job seekers pay for premium job-portal plans, then get fewer recruiter calls than they did applying by hand. One subscriber got a handful of recruiter calls across 6 months.
challenge: Show a job seeker, before they pay, how many real recruiter calls a profile like theirs gets.

title: Re-entering the whole catalogue every time the till dies
problem: Small shops keep switching point-of-sale vendors as terminals break or prices climb, and every switch means re-entering the catalogue. A growing shop that outgrew its till went through 3 systems, paying for each move.
challenge: Move a shop from one billing system to another in an hour, with catalogue, prices and history intact.

title: Firms bought AI and still do the work themselves
problem: Firms that buy AI still do the legal and professional work themselves. Combining many documents into one reliable decision stayed a repetitive manual chore in reports from February 2025 to May 2026.
challenge: Hand a firm one finished piece of back-office work, like a cleaned dataset or a decision memo, not another assistant.

title: Return pickups that never come
problem: Online fashion return pickups are rescheduled for weeks, with false notes that the customer was unavailable. Even after a pickup, refunds sit pending for weeks, and some arrive only after a formal consumer complaint.
challenge: Get a stuck return picked up and refunded within a week, without the buyer spending an hour on support.

title: The tiffin business that breaks at 50 customers
problem: Home tiffin cooks running subscriptions on notebooks and WhatsApp lose track of payments, pauses and dues. This happens once they pass about 40 to 50 customers.
challenge: Give a home food business a cheap, safe step between the home kitchen and a rented one.

title: Hauled the load, then the broker vanished
problem: Small carriers haul loads that were secretly passed on by a broker, then go unpaid when the middleman disappears. Wrong charges take months to resolve and account holds freeze earnings for a week.
challenge: Make sure a small carrier knows who is really paying before the truck is loaded.

title: Small gyms lose money between card and payout
problem: Small gyms pay monthly software fees plus card charges, then wait on unpredictable payouts of their own members' fees. Billing systems lock loyal members out the instant a payment fails and double-charge others.
challenge: Show a small gym owner every rupee a member paid, when it lands, and who is owed what, in one view.

title: A finished edit, locked in by an expired trial
problem: Freelance video editors working from phones find that free editors lack the blending modes, colour grading and transitions paid client work needs. Pay for a trial instead and it can end early: in September 2026 one creator was refused even temporary access to export a project they had already finished. Generative video became affordable in 2025, and an editor who adopts it early can win work that used to need a studio.
challenge: Help a freelance editor deliver client-grade video from a phone, with the export always in their own hands.

title: Money debited, transaction failed, nobody owns the refund
problem: Payments get debited while the merchant or booking site shows them as failed, and each side points at the other. The money can sit for days with no owner and no status.
challenge: Get a stuck refund back to the payer without them chasing both companies.

title: A short walk to the metro, says the ad
problem: Property ads promise a short walk to the metro when the real peak-hour commute is far longer. In September 2026 a developer found unverified listings of its own project on Housing.com.
challenge: Tell a home seeker the real commute, power cuts and air quality for any address in under a minute.

title: Paid for a resume writer, got a template
problem: Job seekers in India pay for resume writing and get generic content. Free features for freshers moved behind paid tiers that do not deliver, a complaint heard from October 2025 to September 2026.
challenge: Give a fresher the resume and job-lead help they were sold, at a fraction of the price, and prove it worked.

title: A personal assistant, but only if you're rich
problem: Help with errands, admin and planning has only ever been affordable for the wealthy. Voice and agent models became good enough in 2025 to make calls, fill forms and book things for someone.
challenge: Give an ordinary person the errands, admin and introductions help that used to need a personal assistant.

title: Salons paying commission on their own regulars
problem: Booking software charges solo stylists commission on clients who were already theirs, plus per-message and per-card fees. The monthly bill becomes impossible to predict, and some owners go back to a paper diary.
challenge: Let a solo stylist take bookings and deposits from their own clients without paying a cut on every visit.

title: The free days the milk subscription never gave
problem: Milk and food subscribers find benefits withdrawn after signing up and offers only partly honoured. In January 2026 a dairy subscriber got only part of a promised free-days offer and was refused help without screenshots.
challenge: Show a subscriber what was promised against what arrived, and get the difference back in one message.

title: Small sellers pay the steepest courier rates going
problem: Online sellers spend up to an hour a day comparing courier prices across zones and weight slabs. They still pay full rates that large shippers never see, and returns cost even more to ship.
challenge: Cut what a small seller pays per parcel without adding an hour of rate-checking to their day.

title: 6 months for a fix, and no way out
problem: Small studios and solo therapists wait months for fixes and absorb new fees added without notice. Leaving feels impossible, because every client, package and booking lives inside the vendor's records.
challenge: Let a small practice move every client, package and booking to a new provider in one afternoon.

title: Translation is either 8 hours or wrong
problem: Small publishers in less common languages get machine translations that still need checking line by line. Agencies are overkill for small jobs, so one website owner spent 8 or more hours per file translating by hand.
challenge: Get a small publisher's video or page into another language, checked and accurate, in under an hour.

title: Locked out after a death or a lost phone
problem: After a death, families spend months reaching scattered accounts, documents and assets because few people prepare. Losing a phone that holds authentication codes can lock someone out of banking and work.
challenge: Make sure the people who need your accounts can reach them, and nobody else can.

title: The co-living room that changes after you pay
problem: Co-living and PG residents face undisclosed upfront fees, unauthorised rent increases and eviction threats. Co-living has grown fast in Indian cities since 2024, and complaints about hidden fees grew with it.
challenge: Let a tenant compare co-living operators on what residents actually paid and got, before they sign.

title: Hiring an accountant, getting a mechanic
problem: Small Indian businesses pay for job posts and get mismatched, duplicate or inactive applicants. In July 2026 one business paid about ₹3,000 for a post and got 11 applicants, including a mechanic for an accountant role.
challenge: Get a small business 3 qualified candidates for a role within a week, without another paid post.

title: Freelance income decided by a ranking nobody explains
problem: Established freelancers with perfect feedback watch client invitations collapse overnight when a marketplace changes its ranking. Years of reputation can stop paying without warning.
challenge: Give a freelancer a steady flow of clients that no single marketplace's ranking change can switch off.

title: The ice cream that melted, and nobody's fault
problem: Frozen food and ice cream ordered online often arrive melted and refrozen. In August 2026 one buyer's ice cream came melted and support offered an unrelated coupon instead of a refund.
challenge: Make a broken cold chain visible to the buyer and costly to whoever broke it.

title: Delivery attempted, says the courier who never called
problem: Delivery agents log failed attempts without calling or visiting, so orders get cancelled while the buyer sat at home. Buyers reported the same story again and again between September 2025 and September 2026.
challenge: Make a false delivery attempt cost the courier, not the buyer waiting at home.

title: Matching aggregator visits to bookings by hand
problem: Corporate fitness aggregators grew fast in 2025. Studios now run bookings, aggregator visits and invoices in separate places, and match visits and packages by hand.
challenge: Turn a month of bookings, aggregator visits and invoices into one reconciled ledger without a spreadsheet.

title: The fake manager quoting double in a creator's name
problem: Over half of Indian creators surveyed in May 2025 had lost brand deals because brands had no verified way to reach them. Fake talent managers fill the gap, impersonating creators and quoting double their rates.
challenge: Make sure a brand that wants a creator reaches the creator, not someone pretending to manage them.

title: Input credit lost because a supplier filed late
problem: Small businesses lose input tax credit when a supplier files late or an invoice is missing from their auto-drafted return. Matching books against returns at year end is slow, and errors surface only when the notice arrives.
challenge: Catch every GST mismatch in the month it happens, not when the notice lands.

title: Housing societies find tank cleaners by word of mouth
problem: Apartment societies struggle to find and schedule water tank cleaning. They wait months for the municipality to prune dangerous branches before the monsoon.
challenge: Let a housing society book, track and verify every seasonal upkeep job from one shared calendar.

title: Hours of lectures and podcasts, almost nothing retained
problem: Learners take in hours of podcasts, books, articles and recorded lectures. They forget most of it within days, despite highlighting and notes.
challenge: Make what someone heard or read this week come back to them at the moment it is useful.

title: Locked out of your earnings with nobody to call
problem: Freelancers can lose access overnight to the account that holds their clients, bids and invoices. In October 2026 one freelancer was restricted mid-bid after paying for visibility boosts and could not reach a single human.
challenge: Make sure a freelancer locked out of any one account still has their clients, invoices and history the same day.

title: Dinner decided at the last minute, again
problem: Hosts planning a last-minute get-together cannot put good food together quickly, because shopping and cooking take hours. Tracking what is already in the kitchen is so tedious that most people give up.
challenge: Make tonight's food plan in 2 minutes, using what is already in the kitchen.

title: Return to origin bills the seller twice for nothing
problem: Parcels come back to small sellers marked return to origin after attempts that never happened. The seller pays shipping both ways and loses the sale, and lost return parcels stay unrefunded for weeks.
challenge: Cut a small seller's return-to-origin losses by half within a month.

title: Small-city patients pay for specialists, get 2 minutes
problem: Patients in smaller cities wait weeks for specialists, so they pay for online consults. These get handed to a different doctor, cut to 2 minutes or cancelled without a refund.
challenge: Make sure a patient who pays for a specialist gets that specialist, that time, or their money back.

title: The sender change that sank a course creator's emails
problem: In August 2026 a course host changed a creator's sender domain without notice. Email open rates fell from about 30% to under 10%.
challenge: Let an educator move their courses, students and emails anywhere in a day, and know the moment something breaks.

title: Freelancers chasing clients who stopped answering
problem: Freelancers face at least one unpaid invoice a month and burn hours drafting awkward follow-ups. They lose thousands to clients who vanish after receiving the final work.
challenge: Make sure a freelancer is paid before the final files leave their hands.

title: Warranty refused, so the same fault gets paid twice
problem: Local repair shops give no warranty on work or parts, and where one is promised it often is not honoured. In August 2026 an AC was still faulty after nearly ₹10,000 of repairs, and the warranty was refused.
challenge: Make a repair or pest control warranty something a household can claim in one message.

title: The tutor who can't say what last month earned
problem: Independent tutors enter payments by hand and split income with partner tutors on spreadsheets. In August 2026 a long-time course creator called per-learner and transaction fees punishingly expensive.
challenge: Show an independent tutor what each student and each month earned them, after every fee.

title: Crossed the GST threshold, and nobody showed you how
problem: Indian freelancers who cross the GST threshold must issue invoices that meet the rules, but rarely know how. Very small firms find even the TDS return due every 3 months clumsy.
challenge: Make a freelancer's GST invoices, TDS records and who-has-paid list correct by default, without an accountant.

title: Kiranas losing their own street to quick commerce
problem: Neighbourhood kiranas say deep discounting by quick commerce is draining their footfall, and they cannot compete on speed. Shoppers who would happily order next-day from a local butcher or baker have no way to do it.
challenge: Let a neighbourhood food shop take next-day orders from its own street without paying to be listed.

title: Parcels stuck in the hub with nobody answering
problem: Parcels reach the destination city and then sit, or loop between hubs, for days or weeks with no updates. In October 2026 a Delhivery parcel sat stuck for about 2 weeks while the recipient could not reach anyone.
challenge: Find a stuck parcel and get it moving within 48 hours of it going quiet.

title: A blood test should not cost a day
problem: Rural patients travel tens of kilometres and lose a day for a basic test. Home packages booked online arrive missing tests, results are delayed, and refunds stall.
challenge: Get a basic blood test done and the report into the patient's hand within a day, wherever they live.

title: The course videos gone in one server crash
problem: In September 2026 an Indian course creator lost uploaded videos for good when the host's server crashed. The same month, a long-time creator's membership account was terminated, taking the content and member list with it.
challenge: Keep a complete, usable copy of everything a creator has made and every fan they have, without them thinking about it.

title: The subscription that costs more every renewal
problem: Small firms find basic features locked behind premium add-ons, hidden costs after they buy, and a price rise every year. One Indian buyer of Zoho Books got no useful answer from support for 7 months.
challenge: Cut a small company's subscription bill by a fifth without losing a feature it uses.

title: When the cook quits on Monday morning
problem: Families relying on a full-time domestic worker face chaos when she quits suddenly, with no temporary help available. Prepaid household help can stay unavailable for months, and working parents lose workdays.
challenge: Find a family verified help for tonight or this week, without a month-long contract.

title: Hiring plans sold hard, then nobody answers
problem: Recruiters buy hiring plans after aggressive sales calls, then face early plan expiry and money-back promises that are never honoured. Verification stays stuck for weeks and support stays silent.
challenge: Let a small employer see what each hiring channel delivered per rupee before renewing anything.

title: The work is done and the money never comes
problem: Money already earned arrives late or not at all. One Indian startup shutdown left 300 staff jobless without notice, many unpaid for over a month.
challenge: Help someone owed money for finished work turn their records into a claim the payer cannot ignore.

title: The vendor who vanishes once the restaurant signs
problem: Restaurants sign up for billing and ordering systems, then support goes quiet and promised features never arrive. When a vendor loses years of loyalty data, the restaurant pays in lost regulars.
challenge: Get a small restaurant from one billing system to a better one in a weekend, with every record intact.

title: Job shops run production on spreadsheets and hope
problem: Generic ERPs cannot handle the work orders and mixed production of a small job shop, so the shop falls back on spreadsheets. Makers raised the same complaint in August 2025, March 2026 and April 2026.
challenge: Let a small job shop see every order's stage and material, set up in a week rather than a year.

title: Tiny ad budgets burned in a week
problem: Independent makers and small brands with tiny budgets find paid ads expensive and ineffective. Money goes out every week with no clear sign of what worked.
challenge: Make ₹5,000 of ads teach a small seller something they can act on next week.

title: The day a PDF invoice stopped counting
