problem: E-invoicing rules reached smaller businesses in India and across Europe in 2025 and 2026. A PDF sent by email no longer counts, so small firms pay a middleman to connect.
challenge: Get a small firm compliant with a new invoicing mandate in an afternoon, not a quarter.

title: Your property back home, and nobody watching it
problem: Indians living abroad fear encroachment on property left empty back home, a worry posted to Razorpay's Fix My Itch in January 2026. Caretakers send no live updates, so the owner never sees what is happening to it.
challenge: Give a property owner abroad a monthly statement and photo update they trust, in their own currency.

title: Paid for a resume, got a train ticket
problem: Small Indian businesses pay job portals a monthly fee and still get candidates living 30 km away. One downloaded 50 resumes and found many were train tickets and blank pages.
challenge: Get a neighbourhood employer 3 genuine, nearby candidates for an entry-level role within a week.

title: Outgrew the accounting package, cannot afford the ERP
problem: Small goods businesses outgrow entry-level accounting and inventory software, hitting order caps and drifting stock counts. A traditional ERP costs too much and takes months, so they keep reconciling by hand.
challenge: Keep stock counts right across sales channels and books, without moving to an ERP.

title: The honest opinion that was a paid ad
problem: About 2 in 3 influencer ads that ASCI checked in India in 2025 failed disclosure rules. Followers cannot tell an ad from an opinion.
challenge: Let a follower check in seconds whether a creator's post was paid for and who paid.

title: The GST threshold you crossed without noticing
problem: Independent coaches and side-gig earners cross the GST threshold without knowing when registration kicks in or what they owe. The chartered accountant they see once a year comes in too late to plan anything.
challenge: Give a freelancer a running view of their tax position that is ready to hand to an accountant.

title: The customer who was never called back
problem: Small renovation contractors cannot see which customers were contacted or still need an appointment. As heat pump and solar upgrades grew in 2025, homeowners named unreliable contractors as the biggest thing holding them back.
challenge: Give a 2-person contractor a job book that keeps every customer, photo and follow-up straight from a phone.

title: Paying for profile boosts that nobody sees
problem: Job seekers pay for profile boosting and still see zero recruiter views for months. Many say they would rather pay for one guaranteed interview than keep paying to vanish into applicant pools.
challenge: Turn what a job seeker is willing to pay into a guaranteed conversation with a real hiring manager.

title: Next-day pay that lands a week late
problem: Small transporters cover fuel and payroll with quick pay, yet Truckstop's next-day quick pay waits 3 to 5 days on document checks. The cheap cash is never fast, and the fast cash is never cheap.
challenge: Get a small carrier paid within a day of delivery for less than a factoring fee.

title: Launched to a handful of likes, then silence
problem: Building software became nearly free by 2025, but solo founders launch to a handful of likes. They have no repeatable way to reach buyers, and most do not know where to begin.
challenge: Get a solo founder's new product in front of 100 people who want it, within 2 weeks.

title: The WhatsApp invoice that arrives blank
problem: Businesses with under 10 staff still work out salaries by hand each month, juggling leave, overtime and bonuses. The payroll module in Tally needs training they cannot afford.
challenge: Make billing and monthly salaries for a 10-person shop take minutes and never fail at the counter.

title: Field crews derailed by an update nobody announced
problem: In India, an independent RO repair professional cannot get their own partner ID on Urban Company. The tradesperson does the work while somebody else's system decides how the day goes.
challenge: Let a solo tradesperson run their own bookings and schedule without depending on an aggregator's system.

title: Payroll errors found only after salaries go out
problem: Small firms pay for all-in-one HR software and still get payroll data errors and income tax computed wrong for a whole year. Support lacks product knowledge or takes a week, so mistakes surface after salaries go out.
challenge: Catch every payroll and tax mistake before salaries go out, not after employees complain.

title: The truck never came and nobody knows why
problem: Small manufacturers book local transporters who never turn up, leaving finished goods stuck at the factory. A container's pickup number passes through 4 hands before it reaches the driver.
challenge: Give a small factory and its buyer a live view of every regional truck booking, from pickup to delivery.

title: Reach that drops to zero with no explanation
problem: Short videos that used to reach tens of thousands now sit at zero. Second posts in a day get a fraction of the first, and creators cannot tell which choice caused the drop.
challenge: Show a creator which of their own choices moved reach this week, using only their own numbers.

title: Cryptic UPI names turn every statement into a puzzle
problem: Spending is scattered across UPI, cards, wallets and subscriptions, and unclear merchant names make small payments impossible to recall weeks later. Budgeting that needs manual entry gets abandoned within weeks.
challenge: Tell someone where their money went last month without asking them to type anything.

title: Shift rosters and hourly attendance kept on paper
problem: HR software is built for salaried desk staff, so shift workers cannot fix a forgotten clock-in. Recurring rosters must be recopied every few months, and every pay run starts with manual fixes.
challenge: Make the weekly roster and the hours that reach payroll match without anybody retyping them.

title: Phone editors that eat a creator's work
problem: Short-video editors on phones lose drafts when redo fails, drop edits when several overlays stack and freeze on export. The saved file sometimes does not even match the edit, so hours of work vanish right before posting.
challenge: Make sure no creator ever loses a finished edit, whatever happens to the editor on their phone.

title: The changelog nobody read until payroll broke
problem: Software makers ship breaking changes with little warning, so customers first find out when something breaks. In August 2025 an HR team on greytHR found features changed without notice and payroll calculated wrong.
challenge: Make sure every customer learns about a change that affects them, in their own terms, before it ships.

title: Share your own work and get banned as spam
problem: Independent makers who share their own work in online communities get flagged as spammers unless they are long-standing members. After generated posts flooded communities in 2025, moderators tightened self-promotion rules.
challenge: Help an independent maker earn a community's trust fast enough to share their work there within a month.

title: Half the workday spent saying what you did
problem: Employees spend hours in status meetings that a short written update could replace. Managers get guesswork, and the people doing the work are interrupted again and again to feed status reports.
challenge: Give managers an accurate status of every task without one meeting or one manual board update.

title: Scheduled posts that quietly never go out
problem: Small businesses pay Buffer and Later to schedule social posts, then watch posts never publish. One was charged a large annual fee right after the trial and refused a refund despite cancelling the same day.
challenge: Give a small business a month of posts that go out on time, every time, with proof that they did.

title: A dozen tabs checked before the day begins
problem: Founders of small teams spend half an hour every morning checking a dozen services for code changes, messages and payments. With a handful of people doing what once took dozens, all that watching falls on 1 or 2 of them.
challenge: Give a small-team founder one morning briefing that replaces checking a dozen services.

title: Lakhs of followers, and the sales never came
problem: A Mumbai skincare founder paid a creator with lakhs of followers for 4 Reels, but sales never followed. Nearly 3 in 4 brands call fake followers a major challenge.
challenge: Tell a small brand, before it pays, whether a creator's audience is real and likely to buy.

title: The shop website nobody has ever checked
problem: Small firms with online stores cannot afford accessibility checks, so people on screen readers are shut out. Since 2025, shopping and booking agents have browsed the web for people, yet sites are built for humans clicking buttons.
challenge: Tell a small online store, in one afternoon, what stops a blind shopper, an attacker or a buying agent on its site.

title: A calm media diet nobody curates
problem: People struggle to stay informed without the stress of the news cycle, and lack an easy way to listen to saved articles. Cheap generative media has not yet become something they use every day.
challenge: Give someone a daily mix of reading, news and listening that fits their taste and leaves them calmer, not more anxious.

title: Job ad budgets burned on clicks, not hires
problem: Small businesses find free job posts get no visibility, while pay-per-click ads always spend the full monthly budget. What arrives is a flood of irrelevant, mass-produced applications, so the cost per real hire keeps rising.
challenge: Cut a small employer's cost per genuine applicant in half without raising their job ad spend.

title: The job offer that asks for a laptop deposit
problem: Job seekers on WorkIndia have found fake tech postings demanding a laptop deposit, while fake coding tests plant malware. Complaints from January 2025, May 2026 and July 2026 tell the same story.
challenge: Let a job seeker check, in under a minute, whether a job offer or test is real before they pay or download anything.

title: Job matches that ignore everything you said
problem: Job seekers on Naukri report that almost every recommended job is unrelated to their profile. Listings marked remote often turn out to be restricted by region, so hours go into filtering roles that never fit.
challenge: Cut the jobs a seeker has to read by 90%, while missing none that truly fit.

title: Every AI conversation starts from zero
problem: People who lean on AI assistants lose old conversations and repeat the same background to every assistant they use. Assistants added memory and project spaces in 2025, but each keeps its own.
challenge: Make what a person or team has already told any AI assistant findable and reusable everywhere they work.

title: A year of building, and not one paying customer
problem: Solo builders spend a year on a working product beside a day job, then stall at a few dozen people. Cold emails to small firms go unanswered in inboxes flooded by generated messages.
challenge: Get a solo builder's working product its first 10 paying customers in 3 weeks.

title: Code ships faster than anyone can check it
problem: Coding agents multiplied how much code a small team ships in 2025, but startups without testers cannot keep quality up. Too often, the first person to find the bug is a customer.
challenge: Catch the bug a small team's AI-written code introduced before a customer does, without hiring a tester.

title: 72 hours to report a ruined crop
problem: A farmer whose field is hit by hail or flooding has 72 hours to report the loss to the crop insurer. Missing that window is the most common reason these claims are rejected.
challenge: Get a farmer's crop loss reported, with every detail the insurer asks for, inside the 72 hours allowed.

title: A ₹2,000 payment stopped by a name mismatch
problem: By July 2025, more than 48 lakh farmers had PM-KISAN payments withheld over incomplete e-KYC. A wrong name on a land record or an unlinked bank account stops the ₹2,000 too.
challenge: Tell a farmer which record is holding up their instalment, and what to carry to which office to fix it.

title: Soil card says less urea, the field gets more
problem: Farmers who hold a soil health card still apply more urea than it recommends, a 2025 Haryana study found. India now uses nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium at about 10.9:4.1:1, against a benchmark of 4:2:1.
challenge: Turn a soil health card into the exact bags of each fertiliser a farmer should buy for this crop.

title: Spraying by the dealer's word, not the label
problem: Farmers mix and spray pesticide on a dealer's advice, and in a 2026 Gujarat survey 91.2% used no protective gear. An Akola hospital treated up to 170 poisoning cases between June and October 2025.
challenge: Tell a farmer the right dose, the gear to wear and the days to wait, from the pack in their hand.

title: The hailstorm warning that came hours too late
problem: Storm alerts often reach farmers only hours ahead, in technical language many cannot follow. In May 2025, hail, rain and pests cut moong yields by an estimated 30% to 45% in 5 Madhya Pradesh districts.
challenge: Warn a farmer in plain words, the evening before, when tomorrow's weather will ruin a spray or a harvest.

title: 8 kg cut from every quintal of paddy
problem: At paddy procurement centres, staff and millers cut kilos from a farmer's weighed crop. In a Telangana survey of 5,000 farmers, 57.3% reported cuts, up to 8 kg a quintal at mills.
challenge: Show a paddy farmer how many kilos and rupees were cut from each sale, with a complaint ready to send.

title: The cow everyone assumed was pregnant
problem: In a 2025 Jharkhand survey, 92.22% of dairy farmers assumed an animal that skipped a heat was pregnant. Only 11.11% got it confirmed, and 57.59% bred animals 6 months or more after calving.
challenge: Remind a dairy farmer of every date that matters for each animal, from heat check to vaccination.

title: Elephants ate the crop, the claim never got filed
problem: After wild animals destroy a crop, only 25% of affected Maharashtra farmers seek compensation, a 2025 report found. Only 1% to 2% got payments that matched the damage, and many did not know the scheme existed.
challenge: Help a farmer file a complete wildlife damage claim the same day, and keep chasing it until it is paid.

title: Booked the harvester, and it never came
problem: At harvest, small farmers wait days for a hired machine and pay more when it comes. In Kottayam, combine rent rose to ₹2,300 an hour and booked machines ran up to a week late.
challenge: Let a machine owner and the farmers who book it share one harvest queue that shows every turn, delay and price.

title: The late train, and the refund claim thrown out
problem: A refund for a train running 3 hours late needs a claim filed before the scheduled departure. Passengers who filed after delays still had claims rejected, in complaints from August 2025 and April 2026.
challenge: Tell a passenger with a late or missed train which refund rule applies, and get the claim filed inside its deadline.

title: A helmet fine, sent to a car owner
problem: A scooter in Coimbatore showed 249 pending traffic fines worth ₹3.69 lakh, many with photos of trucks and cars. In Ghaziabad a car owner was fined for not wearing a helmet.
challenge: Help a vehicle owner prove a traffic fine is not theirs and get it cancelled without a trip to the station.

title: The fake traffic fine that emptied a bank account
problem: Messages posing as traffic fine notices carry a file that reads a phone's bank passwords and one-time codes. A 54-year-old in Pune lost ₹11.66 lakh, and one such campaign infected about 7,400 devices.
challenge: Tell someone holding a traffic fine message whether it is real before they tap anything in it.

title: Visa refused over one missing bank statement
problem: Schengen consulates refused 1,81,111 Indian visa applications in 2025, costing about ₹154 crore in fees. One family was refused over missing bank statements and lost about ₹1 lakh on the trip.
challenge: Catch the gaps in a visa application before the fee is paid and the file is handed in.

title: A broken suitcase, and the airline offers ₹500
problem: Airlines offered ₹500 for a dented trolley and a ₹3,000 travel credit for a bag that came 10 days late. Consumer commissions later ordered ₹17,000 and ₹2 lakh, after both passengers filed cases.
challenge: Help a passenger with a damaged or late bag file a claim the airline cannot brush off with a token offer.

title: The charger that has been dead for months
problem: In a 2025 survey of over 1,000 drivers, 73% of Indian electric vehicle owners had a charging attempt fail. In Delhi, drivers say many public chargers have stayed out of service for months.
challenge: Show an electric vehicle driver which nearby chargers worked today, before they drive there on a low battery.

title: Paid ₹1.9 lakh for holidays that never got booked
problem: Holiday memberships sold at seminars promise yearly hotel stays, then no booking comes through. One buyer paid ₹1,90,000 for 12 years of holidays and was told the fee could never be refunded.
challenge: Help a holiday member who cannot get a booking build the refund demand a consumer commission would back.

title: A ₹10,000 fine for a pollution paper that expired
problem: About 56% of India's 30.48 crore registered vehicles have no valid insurance. In Delhi, over 20,000 fines of ₹10,000 each went out in under 3 weeks, mainly over missing or expired pollution certificates.
challenge: Warn a vehicle owner before insurance, pollution or fitness papers lapse, so a roadside camera never catches them out.

title: The doctor whose degree nobody checked
problem: Police in one Assam district made 14 arrests in a fake doctor inquiry, and 12 more followed in Hyderabad in 2026. Checking a doctor means searching separate registers for different kinds of medicine.
challenge: Let a patient check in a minute that the doctor in front of them is registered to practise.

title: The ad that promises to cure diabetes
problem: Of 332 healthcare ads India's advertising council examined in 6 months of 2025, 82% broke the law against miracle cures. Such ads promise sure cures for cancer and diabetes, and 97% of all ads flagged were online.
challenge: Tell a family whether a health ad makes a claim the law bans, and help them report it in a minute.

title: Every 2 weeks, the family hunts for blood again
problem: Thalassemia patients need blood every 2 to 4 weeks, and families are expected to bring a donor each time. In Chhattisgarh, blood banks meet only 45 to 60% of the monthly need.
challenge: Get a family that needs blood again and again a willing, matching donor nearby before each transfusion is due.

title: Checking the air every morning before practice
problem: In Delhi's winter smog, a 13-year-old missed 5 days of cricket training and a cycling club stopped its weekly 20 km ride. Parents check the air reading each morning, and coaches shift sessions to the afternoon.
challenge: Tell a sports group each morning whether the air allows practice, and when today's cleanest hour is.

title: The payment screen was fake, the goods are gone
problem: Customers show shopkeepers a fake payment screen on their phone and walk out with the goods. One Ahmedabad shop lost a ₹67,000 laptop this way, and 4 garment shops lost about ₹55,695.
challenge: Tell a shop owner the same day which UPI payments never reached their bank.

title: The price that changes at the pay button
problem: Online shops add fees and extras to the cart only at the last step. In a 2025 audit, 75% of shoppers met fees that appeared at checkout and 21% found extras added for them.
challenge: Show a shopper every fee and extra added between the product page and the pay button.

title: The ₹10 pack that quietly lost 4 grams
problem: Small packs are getting lighter while the price on the front stays the same. In July 2026 a ₹10 noodle pack went from 52 g to 48 g, and other small packs lost 2–7%.
challenge: Show a shopper the real price per gram of any 2 packs before they pick one.

title: The licence that lapsed while the shop stayed open
problem: Shop owners miss the yearly date to renew a trade licence, and the penalty can double the fee. In Guwahati, about 42,000 of 65,000 traders had not renewed 3 months after the window closed.
challenge: Warn a shop owner about every licence and permit well before its renewal date passes.

title: You searched for customer care and reached a fraudster
problem: People who search online for a customer care number often reach a fraudster posing as support staff. In Varanasi, at least 114 people were allegedly cheated of nearly ₹1.5 crore this way.
challenge: Tell a shopper whether the helpline number they found is the real one before they call it.

title: Damaged stock, and a claim pending for 15 months
problem: Distributors of packaged goods wait months to be paid back for damaged and expired stock. In October 2025 a federation said some damage claims had been pending for more than 15 months.
challenge: Help a distributor file every damage and expiry claim with proof, and see which are still unpaid.

title: No-cost EMI that still costs ₹1,700 more
problem: A no-cost EMI is sold as free, but tax and a processing fee are added on top. In one worked example from 2025, a no-cost EMI on a ₹1 lakh purchase still cost about ₹1,700 extra.
challenge: Show a shopper what a no-cost EMI will really cost before they tap Buy.

title: 8% wastage on the bill, ₹22,693 gone
problem: Gold jewellery bills can charge wastage on top of making charges, so the buyer pays twice for the same work. In one jeweller's example, an 8% wastage line adds about ₹22,693 to a 20 g bangle.
challenge: Show a gold buyer what each line on a jeweller's estimate really costs before they pay.

title: The boutique's Instagram page, copied by a thief
problem: Fake Instagram pages copy a real clothing shop's photos and take money for clothes that are fake or never sent. In July 2026 a buyer paid ₹7,000 for a silk saree and got one worth about ₹2,300.
challenge: Tell a shopper whether an Instagram clothing page is the real shop before they send money.

title: Advance paid, wedding over, blouse still not stitched
problem: Tailors take advances for wedding outfits and miss the date, because orders live in a register and in memory. One Ahmedabad customer paid ₹4,395 and wore something else to the wedding.
challenge: Help a tailor promise only the dates they can keep, and deliver every outfit before the function.

title: Monthly gold instalments paid, then the shop shut
problem: Families pay a jeweller every month towards gold, with nothing behind the money if the shop closes. In Mysuru in 2026, over 80 people said a jeweller took instalments and left the city.
challenge: Help a family see the risks in a jeweller's gold scheme and keep proof of every rupee paid in.

title: The banned fairness cream still on the shelf
problem: Skin creams with mercury reach buyers through small cosmetic shops and salons. In July 2026 Maharashtra banned 3 creams after 18 women developed kidney disorders, and told every shop to pull its stock.
challenge: Tell a cosmetics shop owner which products on the shelf have been banned, the day the notice comes out.
